subject: general
question: In sexually reproducing organisms, how many versions of each trait does a child inherit?

options.text: Two versions from the mother only

solution: The correct answer is __**One version from each parent**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Sexual reproduction** involves the fusion of male and female gametes (sperm and egg), each of which carries one set of chromosomes. The child inherits **one version of each trait from each parent**. • Each parent contributes one allele for every trait. An **allele** is a version of a gene that determines specific characteristics, such as eye color or blood type. • The combination of alleles inherited from both parents determines the **genotype** (genetic makeup) of the offspring. This may lead to the expression of dominant or recessive traits. • For example, in humans, each individual has 23 pairs of chromosomes, for a total of 46. One chromosome in each pair is inherited from the mother, and the other is inherited from the father. • Traits such as height, hair color, and even predisposition to certain diseases are determined by the interaction of the alleles contributed by both parents, following principles of **Mendelian inheritance**.
